name: Skin lightening and bleaching creams
what_people_do: Apply lightening creams, soaps or injections (hydroquinone, steroids, sometimes mercury) to the face or whole body, often for years, often from a young age.
why_they_say_it_works: Lighter skin is linked to beauty and status; people also use the products for dark marks and "even" skin.

documented_by.source: Skin lightening among traders in Lagos, 2002, West Afr J Med, PMID 12081345
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Lagos traders, 450 surveyed: 77.3% used skin lightening cosmetics, across all social classes; hydroquinone products commonest, steroids and mercury also used; exogenous ochronosis the commonest side effect (2002; this is the source of the "77% Nigeria" number, and it is Lagos traders, not Nigeria).

documented_by.source: Skin lightening in Benin City, 2021, West Afr J Med, PMID 34505500
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Benin City, 454 adults: 55.3% currently using skin lightening products.

documented_by.source: Skin bleaching among African and Afro-Caribbean women in NYC, 2019, Dermatol Ther, PMID 31020513
documented_by.quote_or_summary: New York, 76 African and Afro-Caribbean women: median start age 19.5, median duration 13.5 years; 13.2% used while pregnant or possibly breastfeeding.

documented_by.source: Sagoe D et al 2019, Int J Dermatol, PMID 29888464
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Pooled lifetime prevalence 27.7% across 68 studies, 67,665 people; heterogeneity 99.6%, so the average is not comparable across places.

evidence.finding: 6 products above the US limit of 1 ppm; three above 400 ppm; range 0.05 to 17,547 ppm.

source.name: Mercury in skin lightening products, Jamaica, 2020, J Health Pollut, PMID 32509402

evidence.tested: Skin cancer after years of bleaching
evidence.finding: Squamous cell carcinomas on lightened, photo-exposed skin after an average of 20.3 years of hydroquinone and potent steroid use.

source.name: Squamous cell carcinoma and skin whitening, 8 cases, Senegal, 2018, Ann Dermatol Venereol, PMID 29150154

harm_note: Mercury, potent steroids and hydroquinone cause kidney, skin and cancer harm; WHO calls mercury products hazardous (agent4).
gaps: No tested benefit for the "even tone" claim in this practice.
Sagoe average is non-comparable across settings.
